answers.text: If you put a raisin in water it swells: that is osmosis, water sneaking through a membrane that blocks bigger stuff, going from where water is plentiful to where it is scarce. Diffusion is like perfume spreading across a room, particles wandering from crowded places to emptier ones.

(a) The enzyme hugs the substrate: the active site flexes to grip it, which stresses the chemical bonds until they react, then lets go of the products. (b) Cook an egg and the white sets because proteins lose their shape; the same happens to enzymes when hot, the active site warps, the substrate stops docking, and the reaction slows down.
A plant cell wears an extra coat, the cell wall, which animal cells lack. It also carries solar panels, chloroplasts, that animal cells do not have.
The red blood cell throws away its nucleus to pack in extra haemoglobin, like removing the back seats to carry more cargo, so each cell ferries more oxygen.
